chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever suffers illness for a night, accepts it with acceptance, and renders thanks to Allah for it, it will be an expiation for him for sixty years.' I asked: 'What is the meaning of accepting it with acceptance?' He replied: 'He was patient with what was in it.'

key_terms.قَبِلَهَا بِقَبُولِهَا: accepted it with acceptance (acknowledging it as divine decree)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for being patient with a night of illness in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the immense spiritual reward of enduring a night of illness with *sabr* (patience) and *shukr* (gratitude), equating it to the expiation of sixty years of sins. The Imam clarifies that 'accepting with acceptance' specifically denotes steadfast patience in the face of affliction, reflecting the Shia emphasis on viewing trials as opportunities for spiritual elevation and divine proximity.
